beats.narration: Chapter 6 covers tumor suppressor genes, the brakes a cell uses to stop itself dividing. It carries 212 sentences. 134 were flagged for verification, and 16 of those fell inside my scope, the ones marked false, flagged, or sent up for expert review. I worked 13 editorial findings on top of that.

beats.new_visual_element: One wrong word, traced to its source
beats.narration: The clearest finding is a single wrong word. The chapter calls the relationship between BRCA and PARP inhibitors synergistic lethality. The field's term is synthetic lethality, and they mean different things. Synergy is about the size of a combined effect. Synthetic lethality is a dependency that only turns fatal when both partners are lost. The chapter did not invent that wrong term. It copied it.

beats.new_visual_element: A disease called rare when it is most cases
beats.narration: Here is one that reverses its own epidemiology. The chapter says non-inherited retinoblastoma is rare. Non-heritable disease is actually 60 to 70 percent of all retinoblastoma. What is rare is the event the sentence is describing, two independent mutations landing in the same cell. The mechanism is right and the word attached to it is the opposite of true.

beats.new_visual_element: Another chapter's findings in my evidence document
beats.narration: Now the part I would rather not report. I checked this chapter three times after the first pass, and the second pass found the worst defect in the whole review. It was mine. Most of the narrative in my evidence document had been carried over from a template and still described Chapter 30's findings. My summary table said zero true rows were in scope when there were six. Every section had to be rewritten.

props.costLine: A template saves time until it quietly answers for the wrong chapter.

beats.narration: The same pass re-tested every link, and found three of my own citations had gone bad in a way a status check cannot see. Two gene records and one sequence record are now served behind a bot challenge. The link resolves. The fact is not readable. A reader following it sees a captcha. Those three were replaced. Of 120 links in the workbook, 115 resolve and 5 return a genuine error.

artifactLines: A copied error is still an error, and it outlives its source.
A link that resolves is not a fact that is readable.
My own document described a different chapter for two passes.
Checking the status code is checking the wrong thing.
Where a template saves time, it can also answer for the wrong chapter.

beats.new_visual_element: The viewer gets the same job
beats.narration: So here is what I would hand to you. Take a document you have already checked, and this time check the checker. Open your own notes and ask whether every section actually describes the thing you are looking at, or whether some of it came from the last one you did. That is where my worst error was hiding.
